title: Time-Optimal APSP and Matrix Multiplication in Classes of Linear Neighborhood Complexity
summary: The notion of linear neighborhood complexity is a very general structural assumption on a graph class, covering most classes of sparse graphs such as planar graphs, graphs excluding a fixed (topological) minor, or bounded expansion graphs, as well as many structured classes of dense graphs, such as graphs of bounded clique-width, twin-width, merge-width, or flip-width.
